FINDINGS:
A4-F1 | BLOCKER | refresh-effect-v1 falsely excludes item-duration checks and omits item-grant no-reanchor/no-rewrite behavior

Invariant + authority: ADR0020 Decision 3 requires each selected deterministic capability to declare its operation, required inputs, exclusions, identity/revision and residual interpretation truthfully; integrated transition design 5.9 condition 6 makes that an acceptance condition. The candidate's explicit in-force capability declaration contradicts its actual engine guards. This is a software capability-contract finding, not an assertion that the SRD prints a different rule; an SRD quote is therefore inapplicable.

Evidence at pinned SHA: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:559-570, especially :561 (a missing duration re-anchors the existing timer) and :565 (a supplied duration is not checked against an item source). In fact packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:7533-7557 refuses an item grant's changed duration or moved clock, including an omitted duration re-anchored later; :7565-7613 revalidates item-power durations and refuses replacements without explicit override. The current tool description, packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRefreshEffect.ts:19-26, includes the newer item/grant restrictions but also retains the earlier generic phrase that other effects accept supplied duration unchecked. No waiver changed the candidate or guards.

Reproduction 1 (real source item, live registry): create freshDbWithSession(); createDefaultToolRegistry(), ctx with campaign-1/session-1, seeded RNG and the unmodified getBundledDnd5eSrdPack resolver. Invoke start_effect with {effectId:'a4-duration',kind:'item-power',displayName:'Heroism',source:{kind:'magic-item',ref:'magic-item:potion-of-heroism',effectRef:'c2-drink-payload'}}. It succeeds with a bound 1-hour duration. Invoke refresh_effect with {effectId:'a4-duration',duration:{kind:'timed',amount:9,unit:'day',anchor:'effect-created'}}. It returns effect_error requiring an explicit durationOverride; canonical state is unchanged. The inventory returned in the same probe expressly says there is no item-source check. Runnable scratch: node_modules/.bin/tsx /tmp/a4-probes.ts; output /tmp/a4-probes.log.

Reproduction 2 (real paid grant): give a gray Bag of Tricks, use pull-fuzzy-object, start an encounter with its engine-rolled creature, start_effect bound to gray-bag-creature with the returned bindCreditId and that combatant, omit duration so the engine binds next dawn, advance_time by one minute, then refresh_effect with only effectId. It refuses to rewrite the grant's lifetime despite the inventory's unconditional missing-duration re-anchor description. Canonical state remains unchanged. node_modules/.bin/tsx /tmp/a4-refresh-siblings.ts; output /tmp/a4-refresh-siblings.log.

Reachability/applicability: refresh_effect is in the live default registry and the exported inventory is the candidate's selected capability authority. This is not an unreachable experiment. The runtime guards themselves are correct. The inventory claim is false even though the tool description's later qualifications help the DM.

Actual consequence: reviewers and consumers of the declared capability are told the wrong required-input/exclusion boundary: a typed item-power duration replacement actually needs explicit override provenance, while item-grant renewal can be refused even without a replacement duration. The candidate cannot truthfully describe that capability using its current in-band contract. No state corruption is claimed by this finding.

Sibling analysis: query used: rg -n 'not checked|unchecked|DM.*duration|item grant|grantRef|durationOverride' packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts packages/core/src/orchestrator/tool*Effect.ts; also inspected itemBoundTypedDuration, refreshGrant and durationProvenance in activeEffects.ts. start_effect's inventory entry already describes typed item durations/override provenance, so its wording does not cure refresh_effect. The real sibling probes show a ruling-sourced ward DOES accept a new 9-day duration, and an item-power refresh WITH explicit durationOverride succeeds and records dm-override provenance. Thus the failure is precisely the stale distinction between ruling, bound item power, and bound grant; the runtime should not be weakened to match the inventory. Item grant refresh refusal with override is also present in code.

Suggested closure + evidence: owner is the selected-capability inventory/active-effects maintainers (capability ownership program eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12; reconciliation assigns repair ownership, no other bead was changed). Update refresh-effect-v1 operation/required input/exclusions/residual statements to the actual item-power override and item-grant no-rewrite/no-reanchor boundary, and remove conflicting generic wording in the tool description. Preserve existing source-duration and grant-refresh evidence. A proportionate generalized declaration/behavior consistency check covering ruling, typed item power, and bound grant is preferable to new per-item reproducer tests; existing behavior tests plus explicit reviewed declaration assertions may suffice. No new engine behavior is needed. Re-run selected duration/grant tests and the inventory closure test. The finding blocks truthfulness acceptance until the declaration agrees; it does not request global capability completeness.

Recurrence alias: broad class of o9bd.16 L3-F3 (spend_usage capability/tool description contradicted actual input boundary), different operation and specific cause; registry engine-capability-ownership is the relevant obligation. Not a recurrence of the repaired stack-credit loss or chronological restore defects, which these probes did not reproduce.

NO-REQUIREMENT OBSERVATIONS:
- Remaining rowid ordering in characterChronicle is in the separate registry DB; campaign checkpoint/replay is not its restore boundary, so that query alone does not establish a campaign restore defect.
- Explicitly adjudicated activation context, returned-but-not-started item effects, and unselected engine-pending clauses are not evidence of a missing deterministic capability.
- A second successful use_item call is another use, not a mandated idempotent retry; no general successful-call deduplication contract was established.

LIMITS:
- Census of 115 capabilities is not full semantic/branch proof of all 115. Deep review concentrated on the four ledger bindings and the item/effect/identity/mutation/migration/checkpoint paths named above; non-item arithmetic, advancement, character creation and world semantics were not exhaustively re-audited.
- The 43-selection independent refusal probe covers an unknown argument and exact persisted/RNG conservation, not every malformed value, every state-transition branch or every possible input combination.
- The 53-prefix migration matrix uses one populated inventory fixture, not every historical table/value combination. Existing tests add other legacy/adoption/checksum/failure examples.
- The composed restore fixture covers 63 table schemas but populates only 84 rows; it does not prove every possible state graph or external registry restoration. Existing regression tests provide additional actor/grant/turn-replay cases.
- Checkpoints captured before migration 0053 cannot reconstruct previously uncaptured insertion chronology; this candidate discloses that limit.
- SQLite rollback does not rewind the separate code RNG object; no general failed-call RNG rewind contract was established. The unknown-argument census did consume zero RNG draws.
- No universal source, clause, deterministic-execution, discovery or adjudication completeness is claimed. The candidate's disclosed engine-pending/adjudicated and discovery limits remain inputs, not findings.
